title: Security hardening: pin deps, add secret scanning, and safer default logging guidance
author: Sabrina James
description:
Context: as part of the launch readiness checklist for Quickstart templates, we’re doing a security hardening pass focused on (1) dependency pinning (reduce supply-chain drift), (2) secret scanning defaults in the repo + CI, and (3) safer logging defaults and guidance to prevent accidental PII leakage in examples. This PR does not change the template contract (env var names, telemetry contract) but does change repo defaults and a few example snippets to be safer-by-default.

What changed (high level): Pin dependencies for Python + Node templates: - Python: lock files added/updated for each template; tightened version ranges in pyproject/requirements where we had unconstrained deps (notably web/otel deps). - Node: switch templates to committed lockfiles, and remove a couple of caret ranges that were effectively unbounded for minor releases.

Secret scanning + pre-commit hygiene: - Added repo-level secret scanning configuration (gitleaks) with a small allowlist for known false positives (e.g., "example" keys in docs). - Added baseline pre-commit hooks for: detect-secrets (local), trailing whitespace, and preventing committed .env files. - CI: new job to run secret scanning on PRs; blocks merges on high-confidence leaks. - Updated CONTRIBUTING with remediation steps (rotate key, purge history guidance, notify Security).

Safer default logging (PII): - Updated template logging guidance to explicitly discourage logging request bodies / user prompts / retrieved chunks. - Added a standard note in each template README: "Assume prompts and retrieved documents may contain PII. Log only metadata (request_id, route, model, token counts, error class)." - Implemented a lightweight log scrubber helper in the shared libs (language-specific) that redacts common sensitive fields when developers opt-in to structured request logging for debugging. Default remains: do not log payloads.

Docs and examples changes: - Updated .env.example files to be clearly dummy and to avoid strings that trip secret scanners, while still being copy-paste friendly. - Replaced a couple of snippets that printed full exception objects (which can include request payloads) with safer error summaries and structured fields (error_class, error_code, request_id).

Why now: we’ve already seen early dogfood and Support threads where users copy snippets into production and then log entire payloads while debugging 429/timeouts. This PR aims to remove footguns while keeping the templates approachable.

Testing/verification: - Ran all template smoke tests locally with the new locks. - Verified gitleaks job catches an intentionally committed key and passes after removal. - Confirmed no change to OpenTelemetry attributes/metrics emission.

Follow-ups (out of scope): - Add a docs-site callout about log retention and SIEM export for Private deployments (Kira/Naomi tracking separately). - Evaluate moving from ad-hoc scrubber helpers to a shared "redwood-logging" package once SDKs converge.

Checklist: - [x] Dependency pinning applied to all v1 templates (rag, agents, rag+agent) - [x] Secret scanning enabled in CI - [x] Updated CONTRIBUTING + SECURITY notes - [x] README guidance for PII/logging across templates - [x] Verified template contract unchanged
commits_summary: 1) chore(security): add gitleaks + CI job and baseline config 2) chore(deps): pin python deps and commit lock files for templates 3) chore(deps): ensure npm lockfiles committed and tighten ranges 4) docs(security): update READMEs with PII + logging guidance 5) feat(logging): add optional structured logging redaction helpers 6) refactor(errors): avoid printing full exceptions/request payloads in examples
changed_areas: Templates: python/rag, python/agents, python/rag-agent; templates/ts/rag, templates/ts/agents, templates/ts/rag-agent. Shared libs: shared/python/logging_utils.py, shared/ts/logging/scrub.ts. Repo tooling: .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml, .gitleaks.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md. Example env files: */.env.example and README snippets.

review_conversation:
Marcus Lin (Security): Pinning looks good. Two asks: (1) please ensure the gitleaks allowlist doesn’t include broad regexes that could hide real issues, and (2) remove any README snippets that suggest printing prompts/chunks for debugging.

Sabrina James (Author): Updated allowlist to be path-scoped to .env.example and README code blocks only; removed the broad 'sk-*' pattern. Also replaced prompt/chunk debug prints with a note on using request_id + trace view in Console.

Naomi Feldman (Security Product): +1 to the logging guidance. Please add a one-liner in SECURITY.md about incident response expectations (rotate key, notify security@) and link to internal runbook.

Sabrina James (Author): Added "If you commit a real key" section to SECURITY.md with rotation and notification steps. Internal runbook link is referenced as "Redwood internal" without exposing private URLs in the public-facing doc.

Kevin Osei (Audit/SIEM): For Private/VPC users, mention that prompts can be sensitive and audit logs should avoid payloads; metadata only. Doesn’t need to be exhaustive.

Sabrina James (Author): Added a short note under "Logging" that applies to all deployments; points to "metadata-only" approach and suggests tying logs to request_id/trace_id.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): Concern: lock files sometimes break the <15 min quickstart if installation is slow or mismatched across platforms. Can we keep it simple?

Sabrina James (Author): Kept to standard pip/npm flows; lock files are committed but installation remains one command. Added a troubleshooting note for Apple Silicon wheels and a fallback to the supported python version for the template.

Wei Chen (Docs): Please ensure the README wording is consistent across templates (same headings + same PII warning block). Also avoid mentioning internal-only links.

Sabrina James (Author): Normalized the "Security & PII" section across all template READMEs; removed/rewrote internal references.

Approvals: Marcus Lin approved; Naomi Feldman approved; Kevin Osei approved; Sean Gallagher approved with comment; Wei Chen approved.
notable_snippet: Example README change (applies across templates): "Do not log prompts, retrieved documents, or tool inputs/outputs by default. Treat them as potentially sensitive (PII). Prefer logging request_id, tenant_id, route, model, latency_ms, token counts, and error_class. Use Redwood Console traces to debug content-level issues."
release_notes: Security hardening for quickstart templates: dependency pinning/locks, CI secret scanning, and updated logging guidance to reduce PII leakage risk.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash on 2026-01-21 after CI green and Security/SRE approvals.
